name: b10 — Mathematical Equations, exam-alignment pass (0/15/20)

currentCoverage.note: node scripts/audit-bank.mjs and a direct read of questions.json, 22 November 2026, against the 172 active items (3 quarantined of 175)
currentCoverage.observation: Every one of the 172 active items is linear in its letters: no item multiplies two unknowns, because the contract forbade it until this batch. Depth is also heavily front-loaded — 114 of 172 items sit at depth 1 or 2, and only 25 reach depth 5 or more. The two together are what the brief describes as 'too simple and too easy compared with the actual examination'.

overrepresented: direct-substitution as the solving route (150 of 172 items)
pin-operated as the determining equation (106 of 172)
depth 1 and 2 (114 of 172 items), which is where an item falls to a single simple equation
gaps: quadratic-type reasoning — squares and letter products — zero items, reported first-hand from the 26 September 2026 sitting
divisor-pair search as a solving technique, as distinct from forward substitution
depth 5 and 6 at high (25 of 58 high items)
elimination via a combining equation (22 of 172), and the subset-spanning form of it (official Ex 6) in particular

allowed: integer letter values in 1..20, exactly one solution per letter
chain, star and mixed definition topologies
two unknowns equal to a constant
combining equations over all letters or a subset
review: a letter multiplied by itself (square pin, `A × A = 169`) — ME_CONTRACT.review.letterProduct
a letter multiplied by another letter (product pair, `A × B = 72` with `A − B = 1`) — ME_CONTRACT.review.letterProduct
numeric constants above 18, which both quadratic shapes necessarily carry on their right-hand side
forbidden: a letter divided by a letter
non-integer, zero or negative letter values
an inverted-operation distractor note blaming an operator the system does not contain
a level-2 hint quoting an equation that contains only the asked letter

difficultyModel.metric: reasoning depth, measured by replaying the propagation a solver performs, never inherited from the plan
difficultyModel.low: not generated in this batch — the brief asks for harder material, and depth 1 is by definition an item that falls to one equation
difficultyModel.medium: depth exactly 2; square pins appear here, where the root lookup is the first of two steps
difficultyModel.high: depth 3 to 6, and the asked letter may not be the first letter determined; both quadratic shapes appear, and a product pair measures at depth 3 or more by construction because neither of its two equations determines a letter alone

distractorConstraints.requireWrongVariable: whenever a letter's value is in range and distinct from the answer
distractorConstraints.rejectAmbiguous: any option value that satisfies two error families at once is rejected outright — it diagnoses nothing
distractorConstraints.note: The quadratic shapes add a genuine new wrong-answer route: the other member of the factor pair. It is caught by the existing wrong-variable family, since on a product pair the partner letter IS the other factor.

structuralConstraints.quadraticShare: 16 of 35 items (46%) in this batch, 16 of 207 (7.7%) bank-wide. Two sources, and the second was initially mis-predicted here: 7 slots name a quadratic shape outright, and the slots left null fall through to the index-based rotation in `defaultTargetFor`, which is correct — a null slot means 'no opinion', which is exactly when the default should apply. A deliberately hard batch is the right place for the higher share; what matters is that it did not displace the documented shapes, and it did not: 5 combining (4 of them the subset-spanning Ex 6 form), 9 multi-term, 5 bare pins and 1 pair-constant all survived.
structuralConstraints.quadraticShareGuard: An earlier design put the quadratic shapes into the random `determiningPool` instead. That went badly and is why they are index-placed: both shapes succeed far more often than `combineOver` does, so the retry loop selected for them, and a 42-item batch came back with 18 quadratic items and ONE combining equation — an extrapolated shape crowding out a documented one.

seedStrategy: Per-slot seeds from (generator, section, batchId, tier, index, attempt), as scripts/lib/seed.mjs defines. Append-only: no existing id is touched and every committed item must still rebuild byte-identically from its own stamp.

expectedDistribution.medium: 15 items at depth 2. Named slots: 3 square pins, 2 two-coefficient multi-term, 1 bare pin. The 9 null slots draw freely, except that `defaultTargetFor` claims medium index 2 for a further square pin.
expectedDistribution.high: 20 items at depth 3-6, asked letter never the first determined. Named slots: 4 product pairs, 3 square pins, 4 subset-spanning combining, 2 two-coefficient multi-term. The 7 null slots draw freely, except where `defaultTargetFor` claims them.
